category: 2026 DRC-Uganda-France BDBV Outbreak (Active — PHEIC; deadliest and largest ever recorded in DRC; now spans 7 provinces)
killed: 3,799 confirmed DRC / 2 confirmed Uganda = 3,801 confirmed total
injured: 893 currently hospitalized in isolation (DRC, as of 23 September); Uganda outbreak closed with 18 recoveries
source: ECDC Ebola outbreak tracker (published 25 September) — data as of 23 September 2026
note: DRC: 7,890 confirmed cases across 63 of 167 mapped health zones in 7 provinces as of 23 September (published 25 September; +117 cases and +40 deaths since the 21 September report); 3,799 confirmed deaths; crude national CFR ~48.2%, but roughly 59.7% in North Kivu province (1,480 cases/884 deaths) and ~45.8% in Ituri (6,032/2,764); 1,966 cumulative recoveries. Between 31 August and 20 September, cases fell 26% in Ituri (the epicenter) and 15% in Haut-Uélé, but surged 73% over three weeks in North Kivu — WHO Regional Emergency Director for Africa Dr. Marie Roseline Belizaire said 23 September 'while cases and deaths are declining in some provinces, they continue to rise in others.' Africa CDC's Emergency Consultative Group said 17 September the data 'do not yet confirm that the outbreak has reached its peak,' disputing DRC Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba's 14-15 September claim that growth had already peaked in mid-August. A same-day (23 September) UN News report said nearly 88% of identified contacts are under active follow-up nationally by that measure, though ECDC's own contact-tracing metric (83.4% as of 23 September, up from 79.9% on 19 September) has fluctuated week to week; one in three new cases is still identified only after the patient has died outside a treatment center. WHO also warned 23 September that Congo is running short of health workers to staff treatment centers — a single Ebola treatment center requires roughly 300 health professionals — amid a health workers' strike over unpaid wages in Ituri. The outbreak reached a seventh province (Sud-Ubangi, western DRC) on 9 September: a 23-year-old man who died in Gwaka after a roughly three-week, 2,000km journey through South Kivu, Rwanda, Uganda, Ituri, Tshopo and Mongala; 38 of his contacts have been quarantined, per acting Sud-Ubangi governor Jean-René Galekwa Vundawe. Ebola cases were also detected among schoolchildren in Bunia, Ituri, as the 2026-27 school year opened. The outbreak has now surpassed the 2018-2020 Kivu epidemic's 3,317 cases to become the largest ever recorded in DRC, and per AP is tracking toward surpassing the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic's 11,310-death toll. Africa CDC officials warned 22 August that true case counts could be 2-3x higher (10,000-15,000) given official detection may capture only 30-40% of infections. Uganda: 20 confirmed cases (2 deaths, 18 recoveries) — declared over by its own Ministry of Health 28 July 2026 and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after completing the 42-day monitoring period. France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. A US-convened G20+ Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New York on 23 September mobilized roughly $2.9 billion in cumulative international commitments toward the response, including an additional $267 million from the US (total ~$886-887M, the largest bilateral donor); Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya said 'pledges alone will not stop Ebola. We must be able to trace every single dollar.' DRC's revised 180-day, $1.3 billion national response plan remained only 49% funded per the 15 September UN Geneva briefing, with UN Senior Ebola Coordinator Julien Harneis warning another $1 billion will be needed beyond the first six months. A WHO Geneva briefing on 8 September said the response also needs 1,600 more treatment beds (target 3,000, versus ~1,400 built across 59 treatment centers) and 5,000 more health workers (target 9,000 at 3 staff per bed, versus ~4,000 deployed).
